9-panel cinematic storyboard CONTACT SHEET derived from Image 1. Mix Wide, Medium, and Tight shots of the same scene.

Layout: a rigid 3x3 grid of 9 equal rectangular cells in a 16:9 landscape image. Each cell is exactly 1/3 of the width and 1/3 of the height. Separate cells with a thin black gutter.
- Content must not cross, bleed, or overlap a gutter. No collage.
- Each cell is a complete, independently framed shot — not a crop of a larger scene.

Scene: medium close-up, eye level, Scarlett (Image 2) pauses before the medicine-cabinet mirror with the uncapped coral lipstick in hand, surprised by the color on her skin, Scarlett (Image 2)’s face and moving reflection fill the mirrored cabinet, with the coral lipstick and bright doorway held in shallow-focus background, INT. DOWNTOWN APARTMENT BATHROOM — MORNING, morning, downtown_apartment_bathroom (Image 3), Hard morning sunlight cuts diagonally across the white tile and sink, producing crisp highlights and strong graphic shadows. The mirror catches shifting reflections as Scarlett (Image 2) moves., White tile, pale neutrals, black clothing, metallic silver accents, and vivid coral as the dominant color accent., Modern social-first product photography with tactile, editorial energy. Products shown in real-life context -- hands opening packaging, fingers pressing textures, products on bathroom shelves, kitchen counters, rumpled linen. Close-up detail shots emphasize material and finish. Flat-lays with curated minimal arrangements. Color-matched backgrounds that complement the product. Every frame feels like something you would screenshot and save

Every panel is a shot of the same scene as Image 1 — keep the characters, wardrobe, lighting, color grade, and texture consistent across all panels.

No text, dialogue bubbles, scene numbers, or watermarks.

Reference images define identity — keep every referenced character, object, and location consistent with its reference image; never render a reference image itself as a separate panel or subject.
Image 1 (primary): Primary source scene — generate 9 variant shots from this image
